messages:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] us-west-2 gateway error spike: 5xx rate > 9% over 5m (P1) :rotating_light:
Jenna H: paging oncall — I’m taking initial lead. seeing elevated 502/504 and timeouts for inference gateways in us-west-2.
Samir Patel: ack — joining. what’s the affected surface? hosted API, dedicated, or both?
Jenna H: mainly hosted API fronted by edge-proxies -> gateway. Dedicated pools also showing increased tail latency but not full 5xx levels yet. Customers reported slow responses and a few 502s.
Lee Wong: adding logs from the gateway cluster:```ERROR gateway upstream request failed: 502 Bad Gateway; conn reset by peer; trace_id=usw2-9f3a```
Carmen Ruiz: any deploys in the last hour? I'll check release bot.
incidents-bot: release-bot: No active deploys to gateway service in the last 120m.
Dmitri Ivanov: I’m seeing a correlating spike of connection resets to mlworkers in us-west-2-lb pool. Heap and CPU look normal. Network RTT to workers increased ~20-30ms.
Morgan (SRE): Noted. Could be noisy neighbor on the fabric or an intermittently overloaded NAT TGW. Olga, can you check transit and NAT metrics?
Olga (NetOps): NAT SNAT table saturation on a subset of us-west-2 egress nodes. SNAT used 92% on n-node-azb. Flows are high because of a small set of clients connecting heavily.
Samir Patel: That matches the flow logs I'm seeing — a handful of IPs doing many short connections -> opening/closing quickly. This is causing ephemeral port exhaustion per node.
Jenna H: mitigation plan: 1) apply temporary connection pooling/proxy reuse on gateway (reduce new TCP handshakes) 2) shift some traffic to eu-west-1 as a fallback route 3) scale up dedicated egress NAT instances in us-west-2.
Carmen Ruiz: I'll coordinate the fallback policy change in routing. ETA 3-5m to flip 20% of new sessions to eu-west-1 for non-region-locked customers.
Samir Patel: For config:```curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/routing/weight -d '{"region":"us-west-2","weight":0.8}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN'``` Doing a canary reduce now to 0.8.
Dmitri Ivanov: I pushed a hotfix to gateway config to enable keepalive and aggressive reuse for downstream to mlworkers:```env GATEWAY_TCP_KEEPALIVE=1 PROXY_CONN_REUSE=80``` Rolling via canary to 10% of pods.
Lee Wong: Observability: 5xx has dropped to 6.2% in the last 2m after keepalive canary and route shift. Latency p95 for gateways is down from 2.1s to 1.2s.
Support Pager: Noting customer reports: 4 customers with critical SLAs reported timeouts (IDs: C-3718, C-4032, C-4099, C-4102). Eng contact assigned for C-3718.
Jenna H: handoff for extended mitigation — I need to step away in 20m. Samir, can you take lead for postmortem/scale and Olga continue NAT scaling?
Samir Patel: I’ll take over. Next steps: autoscale NAT pool + add ephemeral port randomization; request capacity increase now. Olga, please confirm instance spin-up.
Olga (NetOps): spinning up 4 additional nat-gw instances: ```aws ec2 run-instances --count 4 --tag Name=usw2-nat-ephem```. ETA 6m to become healthy.
Morgan (SRE): Also enabling short-term circuit breaker to fail fast for upstream mlworkers when error rate > 10% to reduce retry storms, diff applied to runtime-proxy.
Dmitri Ivanov: Watchlist: KV cache hit rates might be affected after routing shift; verifying cache warming on eu-west-1. Pre-warm scripts started.
Lee Wong: Monitoring update: after scaling NAT + fallback, 5xx steady at 2.9% and user-facing timeouts reduced. Still a small subset of requests failing with 504 when routed back to us-west-2.
Jenna H: leaving notes: incident declared P1 at thread_ts 3181590000; initial mitigations applied: connection reuse, partial cross-region reroute, NAT scale. Samir will own full recovery and postmortem.
Samir Patel: Taking over lead. I'll coordinate timeline: 1) finish NAT scale (olga) 2) finish route weight ramp down back to 1.0 once stable 3) run tcpdump on a sample failing path to ensure no remaining port exhaustion 4) capture customer-impact window and begin timeline for postmortem.
Support Pager: customers C-3718 and C-4032 require a customer-visible incident summary — will prepare and email once we have final timings.
Olga (NetOps): NAT instances healthy and active. SNAT usage down to 37% on previously saturated nodes.
Samir Patel: Good. Gradually moving route weight back to 1 over 30m for region-locked traffic. Observability shows steady state.
Lee Wong: Final check: gateway error rate stable <1% over 10m, p95 latency back to baseline. No new alerts.
Samir Patel: Declaring mitigation complete — begin recovery phase and root cause work. Collecting logs and tcpdumps for postmortem.
incidents-bot: Incident resolved — automated ticket created INC-318159. Postmortem owner: Samir Patel.
Jenna H: great work, team. Quick action on NAT scaling and connection reuse made the difference. I’ll add a follow-up to evaluate long-term NAT capacity and consider per-tenant connection quotas. :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: Will schedule postmortem with timeline + remediation items (NAT capacity plan, routing fallback automation, circuit-breaker tuning).
